t: The Primera Junta swore loyalty to the captive Ferdinand VII but refused the authority of Spain's Council of Regency, and historians still debate whether the "Mask of Ferdinand" hid independence as the goal from the start.

The Assembly of the Year XIII freed the children of slaves, abolished the Inquisition, torture, noble ranks and the mit'a, encomienda and yanaconazgo, and approved the anthem and arms of Argentina, yet rejected Artigas's deputies and their demand for independence and federalism.

On 9 July 1816 the Congress of Tucumán declared independence from Ferdinand VII, his successors and metropole, in Spanish, Quechua and Aymara; San Martín's Army of the Andes then won Chacabuco and Maipú, while at home the Directory fell to the federal caudillos at Cepeda in 1820.
dyk: Manuel Belgrano raised the new light blue and white flag at Rosario in 1812 without asking; the First Triumvirate ordered him to hide it and sent him a Spanish red and yellow one, but he had already left for the north and never received the message.
ev: The May Revolution: an Open Cabildo dismisses Viceroy Cisneros and the Primera Junta takes power in Buenos Aires in the name of the captive Ferdinand VII.
On 20 June the First Upper Peru campaign ends in the Disaster of Huaqui; Paraguay has already repelled Belgrano and Montevideo's fleet has destroyed the Junta's squadron at San Nicolás.
On 31 January the Assembly of the Year XIII opens, abolishing the Inquisition, noble ranks and Indigenous labour drafts and freeing the children of slaves.
On 20 June after William Brown's victories at Martín García and Buceo, Montevideo surrenders and Alvear occupies the last royalist capital of the viceroyalty.
On 9 July the Congress of Tucumán declares the United Provinces in South America independent of Ferdinand VII, his successors and metropole.
On 5 April San Martín's United Army defeats the royalists at the Battle of Maipú, consolidating the independence of Chile.
The federal armies of López and Ramírez rout Rondeau's Directorial troops at Cepeda; on 11 February the Congress dissolves and the national government ends.
The Eastern Bank becomes independent as Uruguay after British intervention in the Cisplatine War; the Federal Pact of 1831 follows.

f.founder: The Primera Junta of 25 May 1810, Cornelio Saavedra chairman, Mariano Moreno and Juan José Paso secretaries, after the Open Cabildo dismissed Viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros
f.predecessor: The Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
f.successor: The Argentine Confederation after the Federal Pact of 1831 (now the Argentine Republic); Paraguay, Bolivia and Uruguay became separate states
